Putting the surge in Saudi oil production into context.

Because, yes, Oct 2026 is *technically* the highest since Feb 2026. But only because Riyadh surged output just before the war. Take that one-month blip away, and the Oct figure is the highest in 4 years (and it's among the highest over the last 10 years).

Official Saudi oil data for October:

Wellhead production: 10.563m b/d
Supply to market (net of storage): 9.203m b/d

quotedTweet.text:
Saudi Arabia has been exporting crude so far this month at a rate that suggests the kingdom has lifted its oil production toward the 9-10 million b/d range.

Using both the Persian Gulf and (more importantly) the Red Sea, Riyadh has boosted crude exports during the first 22 days of October to >7 million b/d, reaching pre-war levels (see @Vortexa chart below). Adding clean and dirty refined product, the export flow Oct 1-22 reaches ~8.5m b/d, slightly below pre-war levels of >9m b/d. 

The crude export surge -- and the production boost -- could be part of a "use-while-you-can" strategy aimed at pumping ahead of the potential restart of the war post US midterms (or before the Houthis of Yemen damage another key oil installation -- several near misses already in recent days, including an attack that killed two contractors near a major oilfield).

Note: using Oct 1-2 as typically it takes at least five days for dark transits across the SoH to become clear.

EUROPE’s gas stocks on course to fall critically low before winter ends

Europe’s gas storage has begun the heating season under severe pressure despite exceptionally high prices discouraging consumption and pulling more liquefied natural gas (LNG) away from Asia.

Earlier expectations for a late accumulation of gas stocks as a result of the strong El Niño conditions in the Pacific causing a mild start to the winter in Europe have been dashed.

Combined gas inventories across the European Union and the United Kingdom peaked at 853 terawatt-hours (TWh) on October 27, according to data from Gas Infrastructure Europe.

Peak storage occurred on exactly the average date since 2011 — confounding expectations stocks would continue to accumulate into November.

Stocks peaked about 168 TWh (-16% or -2.10 standard deviations) below the ten-year seasonal average at the lowest for the time of year since 2013.

Storage facilities across the European Union were just 75% full on average, well below the indicative target of 90% and at the bottom of the range set by regulators.

Since then, the storage deficit has worsened rather than improved ...

text:
Honestly, this whole headline is pure noise.

Even without dredging up Vance's track record of faceplants, and looking past how likely this leak is to be total bullshit—considering the source is WSJ and Tehran literally denied it on Tuesday—neither side has any real incentive to engineer a breakthrough right now.

Tehran reads the tape clearly. The midterms were a clean Democratic sweep. They know a Dem-controlled Capitol convenes in Q1. All Iran has to do is run the clock; Washington’s leverage naturally decays, forcing the administration into a weaker hand with far more concessive terms. 

Iran's playbook is pure regime survival; string out backchannel talks just enough to freeze the standoff, avoid kinetic airstrikes actually threaten their heads, and wait.

Could they sit across from Vance? Absolutely. But let him walk back into DC with a signed, bankable deal? Not a prayer. Iran won't budge an inch on its redlines—they have zero reason to hand Vance a geopolitical trophy unless they can skin him alive in the process.

I also can't fathom why consensus is suddenly pricing Vance as some foreign policy messiah. If you parse his post-election drivel on X, it was textbook distance-management (which is laughable coming from the sitting VP, but still). 

Trump is a lame duck second termer; Vance needs to carve out his own lane and consolidate his edge in the GOP succession primary. Projecting gravitas and looking like the adult in the room makes political sense. 

But holding the bag on a toxic deal is completely different. Pulling off even a cosmetic accord with Iran is practically impossible. If Trump dumped this portfolio on his desk, you think that's out of goodwill? Hell no. Vance’s immediate internal reaction is almost certainly: "Fuck, I'm trying to fade this trainwreck and this guy is dragging me right into the blast radius."

Vance has spent every month since March keeping his hands off the Iran conflict, and for good reason. Why march straight into the quagmire now? The moment he inks any paper—even a paper thin PR accord—he owns every single consequence. It’s an obvious political trap set by Trump. 

As much as Vance acts like a tech-right avatar, he isn't that brain dead. And from Tehran's vantage point, Vance is nowhere near guaranteed the Oval in '28—if anything, heavily favors the Dems taking it back. Why everyone thinks Vance is magically going to pull off what Trump couldn't is totally beyond me.
